provenance: navigator-supplied 2026-10-06; a model relevance judgment from the eleven section contracts and data/section-job-canon.json; 'existing' is section contract text, 'supporting' and 'additional_fit' are judgment; filed verbatim from .planning/phases/369.25-feyminto-and-room-identity-spoken-369-3a-the-one-authority-p/369.25-SECTION-COMMAND-RELEVANCE.md; LOCAL prior, never sent to Theo (Canon Part 8)

problem-definition.why: Establish the problem, who experiences it, the intended progress, its causes and what remains unclear.

market-analysis.why: Understand customers, their current behavior, market conditions, timing and adoption.

solution-design.why: Develop alternatives, connect useful ideas, examine the solution's structure and explain design choices.

business-model.why: Explain how value is created, who pays, how revenue works and which assumptions sustain the model. Value proposition already belongs inside this section.

competitive-analysis.why: Identify alternatives, compare on relevant dimensions and test whether claimed advantages survive competition.

team-execution.why: Understand roles, adaptive challenges, missing expertise and who should act or advise.

legal-ip.why: Organize questions about agreements, ownership, protection and regulatory exposure. The contract explicitly records no dedicated methodology command for this section.

financial-model.why: Examine financial assumptions, sensitivities and whether the economic argument holds. The contract records no direct financial-modeling command; these are supporting tools.

opportunity-bank.why: Discover, retain, investigate and qualify opportunities before committing to them.

funding.why: Track funding opportunities and applications, assess readiness, and review a submission against its rubric. The financial model explains the need; Funding manages the pursuit.

strategy.why: Decide where to go, identify what prevents progress, explore alternatives and formulate the next consequential investigation.

meetings.why: Turn conversations into attributed material, identify speakers and reconsider extracted findings. Meetings are sources that can feed several content sections.

people-team-profiles.why: Maintain perspectives and expertise associated with people or generated experts. The repo distinguishes structural team/ from the analytical team-execution/ section.

reasoning-within-every-section.why: Develop the section's argument, examine its evidence and select relevant methodology. These should follow the selected section's job.

research-within-every-section.why: Investigate the question belonging to that section. Market research and legal research share an execution capability but have different purposes and evidence requirements.

briefs-and-presentations.why: Assemble or expose work from selected sections or the whole room. They remain part of the product rather than being excluded as operational.

history-and-continuity.why: Preserve or inspect prior work, changes and continuity. These are legacy command roles, not adoption of their old behavior.

navigation-and-execution.why: Choose, dispatch, schedule or explain work across the relevant sections.

room-access-and-overview.why: Create, enter, navigate and inspect the room and its contents.

quality-and-platform-maintenance.why: Keep the workspace and its capabilities usable, inspect behavior and maintain the system supporting every section.

rule: The section sets the purpose. The current question and problem type determine which command is useful there, not a permanent rule that every section always runs the same tools.
